\[
w_{ij} = \exp\left(-\frac{\beta}{10\,\sigma_Y} (Y_i - Y_j)^2\right),
\qquad
L_U\, x_U = -B^T x_M
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(w_{ij}\): The weight between neighbors i and j
- \(\beta\): The edge strength
- \(\sigma_Y\): The standard deviation of the luma
- \(L_U\): The Laplacian of the graph on the unknown pixels
- \(x\): The probability of the object

Each pixel is a node joined to its 4 neighbors with the weight w, high between similar pixels. Y is the luma from 0 to 1 and sigma Y its standard deviation over the image. A walker at a pixel steps to a neighbor with a chance in proportion to w. Grady showed that the chance x of reaching an object seed first solves a Dirichlet problem on the graph. The Laplacian L of the graph splits into the unknown pixels U and the seeds M, with the block B between them. The chance x is 1 at object seeds and 0 at background seeds. Solving for the unknown x gives the probability at every pixel. Each pixel takes the label with the higher probability.
